sources.entry: nastro - Terminal call recorder for macOS that captures system audio and mic (no bot joins the call) and transcribes on-device with speaker diarization, via TUI or headless CLI.

summary.one_liner: nastro is a terminal call recorder for macOS that captures system audio and microphone input without joining the call as a bot, and transcribes recordings locally with optional speaker diarization.
summary.what_it_does: Records system audio via the macOS CoreAudio process tap plus the microphone, writing audio incrementally to a local AAC (.m4a) file. It offers a TUI (browse, record, filter, transcribe, delete to Trash) and a headless CLI with subcommands such as record, records --plain (tab-separated list), transcribe, and version. Transcription runs on-device using whisper.cpp (default) or WhisperX, and WhisperX adds speaker labels like [SPEAKER_00] grouped by speaking turn, with SRT timestamps. Each recording is stored as a directory containing audio.m4a, metadata.json, and transcript.txt/.srt, with no database. Recording directories are created owner-only (0700) and files as 0600.
use_cases: record a video call without a bot joining the meeting
transcribe meetings locally without sending audio to the cloud
scriptable list of recordings from the command line
keep local archives of audio calls on a Mac
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> && cd nastro && make build
notable: No bot joins the call; capture happens at the OS level
Audio and transcripts stay on the local machine; transcription is run on demand
Audio file stays valid after a crash or kill -9 because it is written incrementally
Transcripts are written atomically so an interrupted run does not destroy an existing one
Two-binary design: Go TUI/CLI plus Swift capture helper with a menu bar recording indicator
caveats: Speaker diarization needs a HuggingFace token with pyannote model terms accepted, a manual step
Building from source requires Go and Swift toolchains
